A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

mGluRs can function as linear frequency detectors of the number and frequency of parallel fiber spikes and that they are involved in a second-messenger pathway that is different from that mediated by IP3 and PKC.

The main takeaway from our work is that
mGluRs in the cerebellum are activated by trains of action potentials in parallel fibers, and they can function as linear counters of action potentials.
mGluRs in the cerebellum function as linear detectors, and that they can detect bursts of activity in parallel fiber inputs.
mGluR at the parallel fiber to Purkinje cell synapses can function as a linear detector of the number of parallel fiber spikes in a burst.
